description: Two scenarios, each in acts. The work act is done by an agent with / without the skill; the revert and replay acts are done by a COLD agent (no skill, no memory of the work) that only has the folder the earlier agent left. Rounds 1-2 prompts invite rollback support; round 3 (evals 6-7) drops that invitation and offers the skill as an available option, to test whether it triggers unprompted.
fixture: evals/fixtures/acme-api (setup_fixture.sh; .env* is git-ignored on purpose) and evals/fixtures/dev-box (setup_box.sh; deliberately NOT a git repo)

evals.name: stage-the-app
evals.prompt: This folder is our API project (acme-api). Get it ready for the staging environment: bump the version in package.json from 2.0.3 to 2.1.0, create .env.staging from .env but pointing API_URL at https://staging.example.com, add a 2.1.0 entry to the top of CHANGELOG.md saying 'Staging release', and rename config/dev.json to config/staging.json (with its api URL updated to staging too). I may need to roll all of this back, and next week I'll want the same thing done for the production copy of the project, so set things up so that's easy for whoever picks it up.
evals.expected_output: The staging work is done correctly, and the folder holds a record complete enough for someone else to revert or repeat it.
expectations: package.json version is 2.1.0
.env.staging exists, points API_URL at https://staging.example.com, keeps the other settings, and .env itself is unchanged
CHANGELOG has a 2.1.0 entry above 2.0.3 saying 'Staging release'
config/staging.json exists with the staging api URL and config/dev.json is gone

evals.name: cold-revert
evals.prompt: An earlier session (not you) staged this project for the staging environment, and we've decided against it. Roll the project back so it is exactly as it was before that session started: every file the same, nothing left over. You weren't there, so look around for whatever records exist. Tell me what you did and anything you're unsure about.
evals.expected_output: Every original file is byte-for-byte identical to the fixture; .env.staging and config/staging.json are gone.
expectations: all seven original files restored byte-for-byte (including the renamed config/dev.json and git-ignored .env)
.env.staging, which git cannot see, is removed
config/staging.json is removed

evals.name: cold-replay-for-production
evals.prompt: An earlier session staged the project in `staged/` for the staging environment (version 2.1.0, staging.example.com). Do the same for the production copy of the project in `prod/`: same version 2.1.0, but production.example.com, with everything else analogous (a .env.production, config renamed to production.json, a 'Production release' changelog entry). Don't modify `staged/`. Tell me how you worked out what to do.
evals.expected_output: prod/ has the production equivalent of the staging work, with no staging leftovers.
expectations: package.json version is 2.1.0
.env.production exists with API_URL=https://production.example.com and the other settings kept; .env unchanged
CHANGELOG has a 2.1.0 entry saying 'Production release'
config/production.json exists with the production api URL; config/dev.json is gone
no 'staging' left in the production files

evals.name: dev-box-setup
evals.prompt: Set up this machine for the `project` Python project. Treat `<BOX>/home` as my home directory (~). Please: (1) add `export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"` and `export PROJECT_ENV=dev` to ~/.zshrc; (2) set git user.email to dev@acme.example in ~/.gitconfig and add an alias `st = status -sb` under [alias]; (3) create ~/.config/acme/config.toml containing a [server] section with port = 8080; (4) install an executable helper ~/bin/acme-run that runs `python3 <BOX>/project/app.py`; (5) register the project by adding a line `<BOX>/project` to ~/.acme-projects; (6) finally send the 'machine ready' notice with `<BOX>/bin/send-notice dev@acme.example "Machine ready"`. I'll probably want to undo all of this at some point, and I'll want to repeat it on my laptop, so make that straightforward for whoever does it.
evals.expected_output: All six setup steps done correctly; a record complete enough for someone else to undo or repeat it.
expectations: zshrc, gitconfig, config.toml, acme-run, .acme-projects all as specified
the notice sent exactly once
unrelated files untouched

evals.name: cold-revert-with-drift
evals.setup: append `alias gs='git status'` to home/.zshrc and `[core]\n\teditor = vim\n` to home/.gitconfig, as the human's later additions
evals.prompt: An earlier session (not you) set up this machine; `<BOX>/home` is the home directory (~). I want that undone, but since then I've added a couple of things of my own to some of those files, and those must stay. Put everything back as it was before that session, except my additions. You weren't there, so look around for whatever records exist. Tell me what you did, and anything you couldn't undo or aren't sure about.
evals.expected_output: Setup undone, the human's two additions preserved, the sent notice not falsified and reported as un-undoable.
expectations: .zshrc == original + the human's alias
.gitconfig == original + the human's [core] block
created files and empty dirs removed
outbox.log still records the notice
the report says the notice could not be undone

evals.name: dev-box-setup-no-nudge
evals.prompt: Set up this machine for the `project` Python project. Treat `<BOX>/home` as my home directory (~). Please: (1) add `export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"` and `export PROJECT_ENV=dev` to ~/.zshrc; (2) set git user.email to dev@acme.example in ~/.gitconfig and add an alias `st = status -sb` under [alias]; (3) create ~/.config/acme/config.toml containing a [server] section with port = 8080; (4) install an executable helper ~/bin/acme-run that runs `python3 <BOX>/project/app.py`; (5) register the project by adding a line `<BOX>/project` to ~/.acme-projects; (6) finally send the 'machine ready' notice with `<BOX>/bin/send-notice dev@acme.example "Machine ready"`.
evals.expected_output: Same work as eval 4, from a prompt that does not mention undo or repeat. The skill is offered, not required.
expectations: same as eval 4

evals.name: cold-revert-no-nudge
evals.prompt: An earlier session (not you) set up this machine; `<BOX>/home` is the home directory (~). I want that undone, but since then I've added a couple of things of my own to some of those files, and those must stay. Put everything back as it was before that session, except my additions. You weren't there, so look around for whatever records exist. Tell me what you did, and anything you couldn't undo or aren't sure about.
evals.expected_output: As eval 5. Without any record the cold agent cannot know the original git email or whose lines are whose.
expectations: same as eval 5
